title: 22 Consumer trend opportunities for 2022 ('22 for '22')
notes: Free page, first archived 2021-12-23 (published on or before that date). Prints 22 numbered opportunities in five groups, each group followed by a summary block for its parent mega-trend (STATE OF PLACE, SOLACE AS A SERVICE, JOYNING, FREEDONISM, META-PHYSICAL). All 27 blocks are recorded in print order; rank is print position, the opportunity number is in note, and section is the parent mega-trend ('mega-trend' for the summary blocks). The 68-page 2022 Trend Report ('6 fully fleshed-out mega-trends', Premium) is not captured, so the sixth mega-trend is unknown. target_year 2022 from the title.

entries.label: LOCALE MORALE
entries.quote: Recent lockdowns strengthened calls to improve the environmental and social fabric of cities.
entries.subject: Brand-led local community improvement
entries.note: Opportunity #1 of 22. Subtitle: 'Made-to-measure communal improvements'.

entries.label: GLOCALLY GROUNDED
entries.quote: But as conscious consumerism gains ground, neighborhood shops stand a fighting chance.
entries.subject: Support for local small businesses
entries.note: Opportunity #2 of 22. Subtitle: 'Boost offline shopping and local connections'. Second heading on the page prints 'GLOBAL GROUNDED LOCALLY'. Section cites a March 2021 survey (53% more interested in shopping locally); present figure.

entries.label: EQUITY ZONE
entries.quote: Consumers expect brands to wade in on front-page issues, but to create measurable impact, it’s crucial to support transformation at a grassroots level.
entries.subject: Brands funding local changemakers
entries.note: Opportunity #3 of 22. Subtitle: 'Become a community catalyst'.

entries.label: COMMUNAL CURRENCIES
entries.quote: The growing dissatisfaction with capitalist corruption is strengthening desire for local autonomy, with crowdsourced communities functioning as a resilient tool to achieve self-determination.
entries.subject: Community and local currencies
entries.note: Opportunity #4 of 22. Subtitle: 'Keeping it in the community'.

entries.label: STATE OF PLACE
entries.quote: Pandemic lockdowns only strengthened calls to improve these localities and make them more livable, community-focused and resilient.
entries.subject: Localism and place-making
entries.note: Subtitle: 'Consumers look to reclaim their locale'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 1-4; the full mega-trend ('20+ sub-trends') is Premium only.

entries.label: SECOND SOULS
entries.quote: It’s now about encouraging consumers to build a long-term, sustainable relationship with the products they buy from you.
entries.subject: Reuse, resale and upcycling programs
entries.note: Opportunity #5 of 22. Subtitle: 'Reuse and reimagine over repeat purchase'.

entries.label: CIRCULARITY SUBSCRIBED
entries.quote: As climate change continues to disrupt supply (even in highly developed countries), the number of power outages around the globe is expected to increase.
entries.subject: Rental of clean energy (solar batteries) amid power outages
entries.note: Opportunity #6 of 22. Subtitle: 'Dealing with life's hardships sustainably'.

entries.label: PRODUCTIVITY PARADISE
entries.quote: Faced with apocalyptic headlines, consumers expect sustainability to be embedded in every product or service.
entries.subject: Sustainability add-ons for wellbeing (slow travel, offsetting)
entries.note: Opportunity #7 of 22. Subtitle: 'When efficiency and tranquillity converge'. Section cites 46% of young people saying eco-anxiety affects daily life; present figure.

entries.label: EARTH DEFINITION
entries.quote: People might want to improve their consumption habits — environmentally, socially, or otherwise — but you can’t be what you can’t see.
entries.subject: Low-impact default options (e.g. standard-definition streaming)
entries.note: Opportunity #8 of 22. Subtitle: 'Small interventions make a huge difference'. Section cites 32% of consumers naming lack of options as the main barrier to sustainable shopping; present figure.

entries.label: SOLACE AS A SERVICE
entries.quote: In short: the impending purpose economy is on a collision course with demands for universal convenience, because instant anything often comes at an environmental and social cost.
entries.subject: Guilt-free convenience
entries.note: Subtitle: 'The emergence of conscious convenience'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 5-8; the full mega-trend is Premium only.

entries.label: LONELI-LESS
entries.quote: With loneliness tied to depression and cognitive decline, it’s time for brands to start tackling this far more stealthy pandemic.
entries.subject: Brand initiatives against loneliness
entries.note: Opportunity #9 of 22. Subtitle: 'Set the stage for human connection'. Section states a third of the world's adults reported feeling lonely in 2021; present figure.

entries.label: SOCIAL EXPRESS
entries.quote: The more locally-minded consumers of tomorrow will want to connect with those in their immediate surroundings, albeit from the safety of a digital interface.
entries.subject: Hyperlocal social networking
entries.note: Opportunity #10 of 22. Subtitle: 'Neighborhood networking for the digital age'.

entries.label: ALTRUISTIC ALLIANCES
entries.quote: In 2022, expect this positive shift to progress in leaps and bounds, with value-driven consumers seeking out empathetic brands that facilitate frictionless connections with neighbors in need.
entries.subject: Platforms connecting volunteers with people in need
entries.note: Opportunity #11 of 22. Subtitle: 'Help your audience help others'.

entries.label: PHYGI-FUN
entries.quote: More than games, they’re spaces to inhabit with friends – early manifestations of tomorrow’s metaverse.
entries.subject: Virtual events on game platforms (Roblox, Fortnite)
entries.note: Opportunity #12 of 22. Subtitle: 'Let's get this (virtual) party started'. 'They' are platforms like Roblox and Fortnite.

entries.label: LINK 'N LEARN
entries.quote: The pandemic has given rise to a new wave of (typically older) digital converts, many of whom are keen to seek out their virtual tribe.
entries.subject: Peer-to-peer online classes for older adults
entries.note: Opportunity #13 of 22. Subtitle: 'Engaging through peer-to-peer education'.

entries.label: JOYNING
entries.quote: As consumers navigate an uncertain future, forging meaningful online and IRL connections will become increasingly valuable.
entries.subject: Meaningful social connection
entries.note: Subtitle: 'Finding meaningful connections in a lonely world'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 9-13.

entries.label: THRILLS & SKILLS
entries.quote: Consumers will relish brands that provide novelty and encourage personal growth.
entries.subject: Playful learning experiences
entries.note: Opportunity #14 of 22. Subtitle: 'Fun for learning's sake'.

entries.label: PLAYFUL PIVOTS
entries.quote: Forget hand sanitizer, tomorrow’s consumers need brands to help them blow off steam, literally.
entries.subject: Brands pivoting to relief and relaxation
entries.note: Opportunity #15 of 22. Subtitle: 'Switch things up for good'.

entries.label: YOUTH GOGGLES
entries.quote: Pure frivolity is a serious part of that process – helping people not only to loosen up, but to see the world afresh.
entries.subject: Frivolity and play for adults
entries.note: Opportunity #16 of 22. Subtitle: 'A new outlook on life'.

entries.label: MICRO-MOVEMENTS
entries.quote: In 2022, consumers will expect you to help them play a role in making the world a better place.
entries.subject: Consumer participation in brand cause campaigns
entries.note: Opportunity #17 of 22. Subtitle: 'Give everyone a slice of the action'.

entries.label: IMMERSIVE INFO
entries.quote: In tomorrow’s even more saturated market, the trick will be to disrupt your channels of communication in unexpected ways.
entries.subject: Unexpected, immersive brand communication
entries.note: Opportunity #18 of 22. Subtitle: 'Communication that hits different'.

entries.label: FREEDONISM
entries.quote: If there’s one powerful remedy to combat the feeling of languishing, it’s FUN!
entries.subject: Fun and hedonism as relief from anxiety
entries.note: Subtitle: 'Fun as the ultimate fear antidote'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 14-18.

entries.label: PORTALS OF POSSIBILITY
entries.quote: The metaverse is teeming with opportunities – yes, for play, but also for personal development.
entries.subject: Metaverse experiences for personal development
entries.note: Opportunity #19 of 22. Subtitle: 'Transport people to new dimensions'.

entries.label: YOU-TOPIA
entries.quote: As consumers enter Web 3.0, they’ll look favorably upon brands that use their influence to build a more egalitarian digital world.
entries.subject: Decentralized, fairer Web3
entries.note: Opportunity #20 of 22. Subtitle: 'Help build a fairer Web 3.0'.

entries.label: PSYCH-E
entries.quote: As we meander towards the metaverse, expect these early concepts to become established healthcare solutions.
entries.subject: VR therapy
entries.note: Opportunity #21 of 22. Subtitle: 'Virtual therapy with real-world benefits'. 'These early concepts' are VR treatments for anxiety and dementia.

entries.label: DIDACTIC DYSTOPIAS
entries.quote: Going forward, brands will use the metaverse to rectify antisocial behaviors for good, by enabling people to (literally) see the world from a new perspective.
entries.subject: Metaverse experiences that change behaviour
entries.note: Opportunity #22 of 22. Subtitle: 'Tough love goes virtual'.

entries.label: META-PHYSICAL
entries.quote: While yesterday’s web was dominated by websites and the social media’s infinite scroll, the next iteration will be defined by virtual worlds, metaverses, and augmented phygital realities.
entries.subject: Metaverse and phygital internet
entries.note: Subtitle: 'An evolved internet'. Mega-trend block summarising opportunities 19-22.
